For a kernel k in L²(μ⊗ν), the operator (Tf)(x) = ∫ k(x,y) f(y) dν(y) from L²(ν) to L²(μ) has adjoint (T*g)(y) = ∫ k̄(x,y) g(x) dμ(x), by Cauchy–Schwarz and Fubini. It does not say where the symmetry of k comes from, which is [THEORY-009](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-009.md)'s question, and it is not claimed for kernels that are not square-integrable. | Active |

| [CLAIM-345](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-345.md) v3 | Equal controllability rank, unequal cost | A9 §2 and A12's Proposition 1 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, the step the owner's U9 "controllability of a system isn't binary" needs. The general statement is the minimum-energy formula with the controllability Gramian. A9: "This is already a standard result from linear control theory." Corrected here: acceptance conditions sit on attainable outcomes, a demand's form depends on whether it demands improvement or maintenance, and A37's weak-preference sets fail only as representations of improvement demands. | [CLAIM-365](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-365.md) v4 | Frustration residual has a simplex dual | A34 §4 and A35 §3 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, checked. The residual is the smallest worst-case shortfall of the declared local improvements ε_i over updates of size at most r. Minimax for the bilinear problem on two compact convex sets gives the dual over the simplex, so Φ_r > 0 exactly when some λ certifies that no update meets all demands (A34's form). Governance regret Γ is the gap between an actual admissible update's shortfall and Φ_r, and is never negative. For L₁ = (θ − 1)², L₂ = (θ + 1)² at θ = 0, Φ_r = ε for every r. The sharp edge: per A37 it is a cardinal refinement of the ordinal fact ([CLAIM-347](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-347.md)), and its magnitude depends on units (A36 §2D). | Active |
| [CLAIM-366](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-366.md) v3 | Shared descent survives reparameterization | A35 §2 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, at the owner's U35 "double click" on whether functionally equivalent parameterizations give equivalent frustration diagnoses. Gradients transform as g′ = Jᵀg and directions as v′ = J⁻¹v, so directional derivatives, and with them the common-descent test 0 ∉ conv{g_i}, do not depend on coordinates. A Euclidean inner product does: g₁ = (1, 1), g₂ = (1, −½) have product ½, and under θ = diag(½, 2)ψ their transforms have −7/4, while d = (−1, 0) lowers both throughout. The sharp edge: it covers coordinate changes of one parameter space at first order, not function-preserving symmetries or training trajectories ([QUESTION-127](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-127.md)). | [CLAIM-369](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-369.md) v5 | Lotka–Volterra is gradient flow on selection | From a synthesis the owner relayed on 2026-10-18 (workbench entry of that date), checked here and given a proof. When competition between components is mediated by shared resources with feature or niche vectors u_i, so that A = UᵀU and r = Uᵀb − c, the Lotka–Volterra dynamics are ṅ_i = −n_i ∂_i L with L(n) = ½‖b − Un‖² + cᵀn: entropic mirror descent on the positive orthant. A rare component's invasion fitness is −∂_i L, the value of adding that feature, and uninvadable equilibria are the KKT points of the convex program. The sharp edge: the identity needs a shared scalar objective, and it fails for asymmetric interactions or processes with competing objectives, which is where an organization stops being an optimizer. Mehta et al. (2019) and Marsland, Cui and Mehta (2020) give the general duality for consumer–resource models. | Active |

([LIT-249](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-249.md)) reach the Hilbert– Schmidt property from a uniform bound, which is stronger. Here the condition is exact: Hilbert–Schmidt if and only if finite χ². It says nothing about what trained features span. | Active |

| [CLAIM-372](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-372.md) | Contextual fraction is Lipschitz in the table | The record's own derivation, from the linear programme of Abramsky, Barbosa and Mansfield ([LIT-265](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-265.md), Eq. 3), which [THEORY-165](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-165.md) holds. Then each connection's maximal coupling makes its copies equal with probability 1 ([LIT-777](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-777.md), Theorem 3.3), so a maximally connected coupling is a joint law of one variable per observable, which is a global section in Abramsky and Brandenburger's sense ([LIT-016](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-016.md), [THEORY-012](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-012.md)). Conversely, a global section gives such a coupling. The two criteria come apart only when marginals shift with context. | Active |

Under A3's one-hop rule I_j = I_j⁰ + Σ_(k≠j) b_k E_kj, with budgets and baselines fixed within an epoch ([CLAIM-282](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-282.md)), an operator's authority does not respond to its own grants. If the collective decision is the authority-weighted mean of the operators' policies, then granting influence to an ally whose policy is nearer one's own than the decision is moves the decision strictly toward one's policy. So the reward for realized policy, and not for held authority, pays for delegating. It does not say operators behave so, or that any rule beyond one hop keeps both conditions. | Active |
| [CLAIM-376](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-376.md) v2 | Instantaneously stable yet positive Lyapunov | The case [THEORY-724](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-724.md)'s source asserts and does not show. If A(t) has first Lyapunov exponent λ > 0, the propagator of A(t) − δI is e^(−δt)Φ(t), so its exponent is exactly λ − δ, while every eigenvalue of every A(t) moves left by δ. Applied to the undamped oscillator switching ω between 0.5 and 3 every unit of time: λ = 0.1955, and with δ = 0.1 the system is stable at every instant, with eigenvalues −0.1 ± 3i and −0.1 ± 0.5i, and has exponent 0.0955. | Active |
| [CLAIM-377](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-377.md) | Fisher equals Gauss–Newton and empirical NTK | [THEORY-084](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-084.md)'s Step 1, stated as the record's own and proved. Through the SVD J = UΣVᵀ, JᵀJ and JJᵀ share the non-zero eigenvalues σ_i² with equal multiplicities, and Jᵀu/σ is the eigenvector of JᵀJ for a unit eigenvector u of JJᵀ. Under y \| x ~ N(f(x; θ), β⁻¹), the expected outer product of the score is β∇f∇fᵀ, which summed over inputs is βJᵀJ, the Gauss–Newton matrix. "Fisher" means the model's Fisher, not the empirical Fisher of observed residuals. It holds at every width, in every regime and on any data. It says nothing about what the spectrum looks like, which is [THEORY-084](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-084.md)'s. | Active |

Since XA always has the column space of X, the GL(p) orbits are exactly the sets of n × p matrices sharing a column space. Theorem 1 is the case of column space ℝⁿ. Column-centred matrices of rank n − 1 all have column space 1^⊥, so an invariant index cannot tell them apart either. | Active |

For b > 0, K_X and the Gram matrix XXᵀ determine each other, by a monotone map on the shared eigenvalues; and equal Gram matrices mean an orthogonal transformation ([CLAIM-290](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-290.md), [THEORY-004](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-004.md)). For b = 0, K_X is the projection onto the column space, which fixes X only up to an invertible linear map, as for a softmax layer ([THEORY-723](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-723.md)). | Active |
| [CLAIM-382](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-382.md) v2 | Autoencoder representations are rotation-invariant | [THEORY-288](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-288.md)'s symmetry argument, stated as the record's own and proved. Transform the parameters by orthogonal maps Q_l of the hidden spaces that commute with the activation. The network then computes Q_l h_l and the same output, so the loss is invariant. Gradient steps commute with the transformation, and an i.i.d. Gaussian initialisation is invariant under it, so the law of the trained representations is too. For radial activations this is all of O(n), and no basis is privileged in law. For elementwise ones it is a finite group, so the axes may be privileged. Whether they are, and how strongly, is [THEORY-288](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-288.md)'s empirical content. The argument needs an orthogonally equivariant optimiser, and fails for Adam. | Active |
| [CLAIM-383](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-383.md) v3 | Shear flows have transient growth at least cR | [THEORY-304](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-304.md)'s scalings as lower bounds, derived. At streamwise wavenumber zero, the cross-stream velocities obey an R-independent Stokes problem in the time t/R. They force the streamwise velocity through −U′v, so the streamwise response is R times an R-independent field. In the energy norm this gives transient growth at least cR, and in the steady forced problem a resolvent norm at least cR². Through pseudospectra, a perturbation of norm O(R⁻²) then moves an eigenvalue into the unstable half-plane wherever the flow is eigenvalue-stable. The sharp constants, and that the growth is no more than order R, come from the computation and are not here. | Active |

| [CLAIM-409](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-409.md) v3 | Sufficiency deficiency is monotone, closure isn't | Two readers' drafts of one point, from A6, A7, A16 and A17 of the exchange of 2026-10-20. A16 §5 and A17's Proposition 2: a fixed-target deficiency is refinement-monotone; "Adding information cannot hurt exact sufficiency for an unchanged question, but changing what the description is expected to explain can expose new dependencies." A6 §6 and A7's Proposition 3: "Increasing the information retained by a representation can destroy a desirable dynamical property", and "There is no general data-processing inequality ordering these quantities, because both the predicted variable and the conditioning information change." This claim joins them, and corrects A7's slogan "When More Information Reveals Less Autonomy": closure is not reversed by refinement, it is unordered by it. Checked exactly on 2026-10-21. | Active |
| [CLAIM-414](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-414.md) v5 | Matched trajectories can hide efficacy | A10 of the exchange on experience and interpretation, re-run here. Three one-bit systems behave alike when the interpretation is 0. Under an intervention that sets it to 1, the first never acts on it, the second acts at once, and the third acts one step late, because its own interpretation opens the gate. Two two-constraint systems have the same trajectory, (1,1) throughout. A single perturbation runs one into (0,0) and leaves the other restored to (1,1): one maintains its constraints by [CLAIM-395](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-395.md)'s minimal slow–fast closure, the other is reset from outside. These are [CLAIM-407](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-407.md)'s lesson about governance and [CLAIM-194](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-194.md)'s about boundaries, applied to interpretation. | Active |
| [CLAIM-434](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-434.md) | A potential exists iff winning moves are acyclic | The formal core of the rename of 2026-10-23 from "ascendancy" to "potential" ([TERM-076](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-076.md)). Part 1 is the finite case of Monderer and Shapley's equivalence between the finite improvement property and a generalized ordinal potential, proved here because the record has not read their paper ([LIT-1462](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1462.md)). Part 2 is a calibration of the Hodge decomposition (Candogan et al.; Jiang et al.) for binary conflict records, computed here: even a perfect ranking leaves a cyclic residual. Part 3 separates coherence from alignment. Parts 9 to 11 were added after a second review. Parts 4 to 8 were added when a review of the pull request found that the measures built on parts 2 and 3 confused ordinal and cardinal structure; each is checked in scratch/formal/valence.py. | Active |
| [CLAIM-436](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-436.md) v5 | Orderings need not be a common currency | The formal half of the owner's reframing of 2026-10-23, that a "common currency" is better read as a negotiation admitting an (at least instantaneous) ordering. On finite option sets the two coincide at each instant. On a continuum they do not: a graded lexicographic order, one form ALARM's "100% weight" override could take, admits no numerical representation, while a continuous ordering, the form of Veit's proportional trade-offs, admits a continuous one (Eilenberg; Debreu). A threshold override admits a discontinuous one, and one with a discrimination threshold, a lexicographic semiorder, can cycle and admits no ordering at all (Luce; Tversky). Across instants, representations need not be related, so a sequence of currencies need not be one currency. | Active |
| [CLAIM-480](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-480.md) v2 | Composition turns an interior into a constraint | From A22 §4 and A23 §IV of the exchange of 2026-10-27, which called composition "the most important missing mechanism" after the owner's U20. Eliminating an equilibrated interior leaves an effective boundary relation that no part has; an outside system interacting only with the boundary meets it as a constraint, and "The interior has effectively become apparatus." | [CLAIM-581](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-581.md) v4 | Transition threshold is a pseudo-ultrametric | The assistant's own proposition, filed on 2026-11-05 at the owner's invitation to contribute. Take configurations joined by reversible moves, each move with a peak requirement, and let d(x, y) be the least, over paths, of the largest requirement on the path ([CLAIM-571](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-571.md)'s threshold, identities free). Concatenating a path from x to y with one from y to z has peak max(d(x, y), d(y, z)), so d(x, z) ≤ max(d(x, y), d(y, z)): d is an extended pseudo-ultrametric (distinct states joined at no cost are at distance 0, unjoined ones at ∞; it is an ultrametric only when every pair of distinct states is separated by a positive cost). Hence at each budget b, "x and y can be turned into one another within b" is an equivalence relation, its classes are the components of the budget-b move graph, and as b grows the classes only merge, forming one dendrogram, the merge tree of zero-dimensional sublevel persistence (Mirth et al.). Under additive costs d is a metric and budgeted identification is intransitive in general. Along a tree, PMI additivity is therefore the same thing as piecewise constancy on the finest groups: it has content only where attributes cross-cut, as in analogy families. For fixed configurations Ω and fixed response laws, let π(Q) be the partition of Ω into classes no probe in Q separates. Then π(Q1 ∪ Q2) is the meet (common refinement) of π(Q1) and π(Q2), while π(Q1 ∩ Q2) is at least as coarse as their join and can be strictly coarser. So π is order-reversing and meet-preserving, its image is a meet-closed part of the partition lattice and need not be a sublattice, and with m probes it has at most 2^m members, against Bell(\|Ω\|) partitions (32 against 115,975 for m = 5 and \|Ω\| = 10).
